description: Selected voyages and unresolved phases from the Americas, Arctic and Antarctica. Dates retain the precision of their sources. This inventory supplements the dated itinerary catalog.

entries.name: Cabot’s Matthew
entries.note: Accounts disagree on the Bristol departure day and the North American landfall is unresolved. Keep the observed date and geographic uncertainty together.

anchors.name: Bristol departure
anchors.note: Sources place the departure in May but disagree on the day.

anchors.name: Eastern North American coast, unidentified landfall
anchors.note: Cape Breton, Newfoundland and additional sites have been proposed. No single point represents the landfall.

anchors.name: Bristol return
anchors.note: Contemporary chronology as reported by Newfoundland and Labrador Heritage.

entries.name: Cabot’s subsequent fleet
entries.note: Records attest a departure and uncertain outcome. Keep as incomplete archival evidence.

entries.name: Roberval and France-Roi
entries.note: Roberval left Newfoundland on 30 June 1542 and reached Cap-Rouge at the end of July. The end-of-July report does not establish a day.

anchors.name: Newfoundland departure
anchors.note: Newfoundland departure in the museum history.

anchors.name: Cap-Rouge arrival
anchors.note: Reported in the latter part of July.

entries.name: Cook’s third voyage · Clerke and Gore return
entries.note: Clerke took over after Cook’s death, returned to the Bering Sea and died on the voyage. Gore led the homeward voyage. Extract a separate track by command.

entries.name: Columbus’s third voyage · Paria and Hispaniola
entries.note: Primary account supports the Paria exploration and later Hispaniola stay. Verify explicit island, coast and removal dates before drawing a detailed leg.

entries.name: Columbus’s fourth voyage · Jamaica and return
entries.note: The Jamaica stay began in June 1503, and the return to Spain was in November 1504. The precise interval endpoints still need reconciliation with the account conventions.

entries.name: Franklin expedition · Beechey Island winter and Inuit accounts
entries.note: A documented seasonal stay lacks a demonstrated exact ship arrival and departure here. Inuit testimony about the expedition’s late movements is evidence in its own right and should retain its stated precision.

entries.name: Franklin expedition · ship abandonment
entries.note: The day is explicit, but the vessels’ positions at abandonment are not established by the initial 1846 pack-ice position or by modern wreck coordinates.

entries.name: Robert McClure’s Investigator and rescue
entries.note: First recorded traverse of the Northwest Passage by a combination of ship and sledge. Preserve the abandonment and relief expedition as a separate leg.

entries.name: Sverdrup’s second Fram expedition
entries.note: Three winters around southern Ellesmere Island supported extensive surveys. Extract winter bases and sledge dates from the expedition diaries.

entries.name: Frederick Cook’s North Pole claim
entries.note: Cook claimed a North Pole date of 21 April 1908. Treat it as a disputed historical claim, with verified travel anchors separate from the alleged pole position.

entries.name: Robert Peary and Matthew Henson expedition
entries.note: Peary claimed the North Pole on 6 April 1909, with Matthew Henson and Inuit expedition members. The claim remains contested. The Library of Congress timeline contains a year typo for the claimed April event. Use the Fram Museum narrative for 1909.

entries.name: Amundsen, Ellsworth and Nobile · Norge airship crossing
entries.note: Mapped in norge-transpolar-flight-1926 using air mode.

anchors.name: North Pole overflight
anchors.note: Airship passed over the North Pole.

entries.name: Byrd and Balchen · first South Pole overflight
entries.note: Mapped in byrd-south-pole-flight-1929 using air mode. Same-day return is described in the South Pole stop note.

anchors.name: Little America departure
anchors.note: The Floyd Bennett took off from Little America.

anchors.name: South Pole overflight
anchors.note: The aircraft flew over the Pole and returned to Little America.

entries.name: Amundsen and Sverdrup · Maud expedition
entries.note: Long drifting study after the Northeast Passage, with different personnel and air operations. Recover the museum’s dated positions and keep routes distinct.

entries.name: Lincoln Ellsworth’s initial Antarctic flight expeditions
entries.note: The 1933–34 aircraft was damaged on pack ice. The 1934 season did not complete the crossing. The successful transcontinental flight occurred in 1935 beyond the atlas endpoint.

entries.name: Borchgrevink’s Ross Ice Shelf ski journey
entries.note: An approximate farthest-south latitude is supported. The selected source provides the month and a range of possible latitudes.

entries.name: Bransfield, Smith and Palmer · early Antarctic Peninsula reports
entries.note: Different expeditions and dates figure in continental-sighting priority accounts. Keep offshore sightings separate from landing claims.

entries.name: Biscoe, Kemp and Balleny · sealing-era Antarctic surveys
entries.note: Separate expeditions that investigated Antarctic islands and possible coastline. Recover voyage logs before adding route geometry.

entries.name: Dumont d’Urville · Astrolabe and Zélée
entries.note: French expedition overlapped the Wilkes survey and included Antarctic rock sampling. Extract dated observation and landing positions separately.

entries.name: Southern Cross contemporaries and later national expeditions
entries.note: Add Valdivia, Gauss, Scotia, both Charcot expeditions, Shirase’s Kainan Maru, Filchner’s Deutschland and Mawson’s Australasian Antarctic Expedition as separate routes after phase-level source extraction.

entries.name: Shackleton–Rowett expedition · Quest
entries.note: Shackleton’s outward leg and endpoint are mapped. The later Wild-led ship track is held.

entries.name: Mawson · BANZARE
entries.note: Selected dated continental landings are mapped. Aircraft observations require a separately sourced route.

entries.name: Aurora’s unplanned Ross Sea pack drift
entries.note: Aurora was driven away from Cape Evans, stranding the shore party. It drifted under Stenhouse and later reached New Zealand. Further extraction should use the ship log and georeference distinct drift stages.

entries.name: Swedish Antarctic expedition · Antarctic shipwreck, Hope Bay and Paulet groups
entries.note: The landing, sinking and journeys of three groups need separate route identities. Göteborg University confirms convergence at Snow Hill and rescue. Ship and party dates should be tied to the corresponding journals.

entries.name: Iberian Atlantic and Caribbean expeditions
entries.note: Further candidates include Ojeda/de la Cosa/Vespucci, Vicente Yáñez Pinzón, Pedro Álvares Cabral, the Corte-Real voyages, Bastidas, Solís and Ponce de León. Keep Vespucci’s disputed voyages and uncertain landfalls separate from dated archival evidence.

entries.name: Spanish coastal expeditions and inland crossings
entries.note: Balboa is already a year-level atlas event. Prioritize Hernández de Córdoba, Grijalva, Cortés, Narváez, Cabeza de Vaca, de Soto and Coronado by dated voyage, land expedition, or forced movement.

entries.name: Verrazzano, Basque whaling, Frobisher, Davis and Baffin
entries.note: Distinguish individual voyages, recurring commercial activity, and uncertain landfall identifications. Cartier and Hudson have their own draft rows.

entries.name: Marquette and Jolliet · Mississippi watershed
entries.note: The May 17 departure and June 17 Mississippi entry are mapped. A continuous route through the Fox and Wisconsin rivers and the downstream return require additional anchors.

entries.name: Alexander Mackenzie and Indigenous guides
entries.note: The journeys are mapped as separate voyages, each with exact-day start and destination evidence. Intermediate canoe, walking and portage legs and return journeys remain to be extracted.

entries.name: Spanish Pacific Northwest survey voyages
entries.note: Prioritize Pérez; Heceta, Bodega y Quadra and Mourelle; Arteaga and Bodega; Martínez and Haro; Eliza, Fidalgo and Quimper; Galiano and Valdés. A dated Malaspina route is supplied independently.

entries.name: La Pérouse voyage · Vanikoro wrecks
entries.note: Wreck evidence identifies Vanikoro, but the day is unknown. Avoid a dated final marker.

anchors.name: Vanikoro wreck area
anchors.note: Regional wreck location. The day of loss is unknown.

entries.name: Malaspina’s disputed-day Nootka and omitted survey ports
entries.note: The U.S. National Archives cites 12 or 13 August 1791 for Nootka arrival. A two-day uncertainty window is appropriate once supported. Visit month and day precision must be verified leg by leg.

anchors.name: Nootka Sound
anchors.note: Arrival occurred on one of the two days.

entries.name: Frobisher’s first voyage · Baffin Island phase
entries.note: Departure and the Greenland sighting are mapped. The subsequent Baffin Island leg appears in the date-band index pending stronger day-and-location matching.

entries.name: Verrazzano’s coast survey after the New York Harbor entry
entries.note: Key dates support departure and the harbor entry. Narragansett Bay and the northern coastal survey remain held at broader date precision.
